name: io.github.aidatatools-dev/astro-agents
title: Astro Agents - research-grade astronomical data API
description: Research-grade astronomical data API: NASA/JPL DE440 ephemerides, any date, SHA-256 verifiable.

tools.name: rise_set_times
tools.description: Sunrise, sunset, moonrise, moonset and twilight times for a place and date: rise, transit and set of the Sun, Moon and planets, civil/nautical/astronomical dawn and dusk, day length, golden hour and blue hour, in UTC and local time. E.g. {date: '2026-06-21', latitude: 48.8566, longitude: 2.3522}. For sky, weather, photography and outdoor apps: for one local calendar day at a place (time zone and DST resolved from the coordinates), each body's rise and set (with azimuth) and upper transit (with altitude), or 'always_up' / 'always_down' when it neither rises nor sets (polar day and night); for the Sun, dawn and dusk at -6, -12 and -18 degrees, solar noon, day length, and the golden hour (Sun between -4 and +6 degrees) and blue hour (-6 to -4) intervals. Times in UTC to the second, local time with its offset, and unix timestamps; every convention (refraction, limb, horizon) is in result.settings. Deterministic (JPL DE440, no LLM); every result carries meta.result_sha256. Price $0.01 per call via REST POST https://astro-agent.dev/v1/astronomy/rise-set (x402 or MPP); each client gets 1 free call on the $0.01-0.02 tools, this one included.

date.description: The local calendar day at the place, YYYY-MM-DD (1800-01-02..2199-12-30), midnight to midnight in its time zone.

elevation_m.description: Height above the WGS84 ellipsoid, metres (no terrain or horizon dip is modelled).

timezone.description: IANA zone for local times, e.g. 'Europe/Paris'. Optional: resolved from the coordinates (with its historical DST rules).

bodies.description: Bodies to time. Default: all ten (Sun, Moon, Mercury..Pluto). The Sun's twilight block is always returned.

tools.name: altitude_azimuth
tools.description: Where the Sun, Moon and planets are in the sky from a place at a moment: altitude, azimuth, compass point, topocentric right ascension and declination, distance, elongation, illumination, magnitude and the sky state. E.g. {datetime: '2026-06-21T23:00', latitude: 48.8566, longitude: 2.3522}. For sky maps, telescope pointing, AR and observation apps: each body's apparent altitude and azimuth (with refraction, or airless), whether it is above the horizon, its topocentric right ascension and declination, distance (and the Moon's in km), angular distance from the Sun, illuminated fraction and visual magnitude (planets), plus the sky state (day, civil / nautical / astronomical twilight, night). Matches NASA/JPL Horizons to under a second of arc. Deterministic (JPL DE440, no LLM); every result carries meta.result_sha256. Price $0.01 per call via REST POST https://astro-agent.dev/v1/astronomy/altaz (x402 or MPP); each client gets 1 free call on the $0.01-0.02 tools, this one included.

datetime.description: The moment: UTC ('2026-06-21T21:00:00Z'), with an explicit offset, or local civil time at the place ('2026-06-21T23:00', time zone resolved from the coordinates).

elevation_m.description: Height above the WGS84 ellipsoid, metres (no terrain or horizon dip is modelled).

timezone.description: IANA zone for local times, e.g. 'Europe/Paris'. Optional: resolved from the coordinates (with its historical DST rules).

bodies.description: Bodies to locate. Default: all ten.

refraction.description: Apply atmospheric refraction to the altitude (true) or give the geometric, airless altitude (false).

temperature_c.description: Air temperature for refraction, deg C.

pressure_hpa.description: Air pressure for refraction, hPa, or 'standard' (from the elevation).

tools.name: observation_windows
tools.description: Which planets and the Moon can be observed tonight from a place, and when: windows above a minimum altitude while the sky is dark, with the best time, altitude, azimuth and magnitude. E.g. {date: '2026-06-21', latitude: 48.8566, longitude: 2.3522}. For observation planning: over the night that starts on 'date' (local noon to noon), the intervals when each body stands at least min_altitude_deg above the horizon while the Sun is at or below sun_altitude_max_deg (default -6: after civil dusk), each with start, end, duration and the best moment (highest altitude) with its azimuth and visual magnitude; plus the dark interval itself. Deterministic (JPL DE440, no LLM); every result carries meta.result_sha256. Price $0.02 per call via REST POST https://astro-agent.dev/v1/astronomy/visibility (x402 or MPP); each client gets 1 free call on the $0.01-0.02 tools, this one included.

date.description: The evening that starts the observing night, YYYY-MM-DD: the night runs from local noon on that date to local noon the next day.

elevation_m.description: Height above the WGS84 ellipsoid, metres (no terrain or horizon dip is modelled).

timezone.description: IANA zone for local times, e.g. 'Europe/Paris'. Optional: resolved from the coordinates (with its historical DST rules).

bodies.description: Bodies to plan. Default: the Moon and Mercury..Neptune.

min_altitude_deg.description: Lowest useful altitude of the body above the horizon, degrees.

sun_altitude_max_deg.description: The sky counts as dark when the Sun is at or below this altitude: -6 civil, -12 nautical, -18 astronomical.

tools.name: moon_details
tools.description: Moon phase today and in detail: phase name and angle, illuminated fraction, age, distance, apparent size, the next new, quarter and full Moons, and the next perigee and apogee; with a place, moonrise and moonset. E.g. {datetime: '2026-01-03T12:00:00Z'}. For calendar, weather, photography and tide apps: phase (8 names), phase angle, illuminated fraction, waxing or waning, age in days since the new Moon, Brown lunation number, centre-to-centre distance in km and Earth radii, angular diameter, ecliptic position, the previous new Moon, the next four principal phases and the next perigee and apogee with their distances, to the second. With latitude/longitude: the Moon's altitude and azimuth there and that local day's moonrise, transit and moonset. Perigee and apogee match NASA/JPL Horizons to the minute. Deterministic (JPL DE440, no LLM); every result carries meta.result_sha256. Price $0.01 per call via REST POST https://astro-agent.dev/v1/astronomy/moon (x402 or MPP); each client gets 1 free call on the $0.01-0.02 tools, this one included.

datetime.description: The moment: UTC, an explicit offset, or local civil time at the place given by latitude/longitude. Default: now (UTC, to the minute).

latitude.description: Optional: add the Moon's altitude and azimuth from this place and that local day's moonrise, transit and moonset.

elevation_m.description: Height above the WGS84 ellipsoid, metres (no terrain or horizon dip is modelled).

timezone.description: IANA zone for local times, e.g. 'Europe/Paris'. Optional: resolved from the coordinates (with its historical DST rules).

tools.name: day_summary
tools.description: Today's sky for a place in one call: sunrise, sunset, twilight, golden and blue hour, the Moon's phase and moonrise, the planets visible tonight, the next lunations and the next eclipse. E.g. {date: '2026-08-10', latitude: 48.8566, longitude: 2.3522}. The daily sky block of a weather, calendar or outdoor app, in one request: the Sun (rise, solar noon, set, civil / nautical / astronomical dawn and dusk, day length, golden and blue hour), the Moon (phase, illuminated fraction, age, distance, moonrise, transit, moonset, the next principal phase), the planets observable that night (window, best time, altitude, azimuth, magnitude; brightest first), the lunations and planetary stations of the next 7 days, and the next solar or lunar eclipse anywhere on Earth. Local times with offset, UTC and unix timestamps; each block follows the conventions of its own route. Deterministic (JPL DE440, no LLM); every result carries meta.result_sha256. Price $0.02 per call via REST POST https://astro-agent.dev/v1/astronomy/day (x402 or MPP); each client gets 1 free call on the $0.01-0.02 tools, this one included.

date.description: The local calendar day at the place, YYYY-MM-DD (1800-01-02..2199-12-30).

elevation_m.description: Height above the WGS84 ellipsoid, metres (no terrain or horizon dip is modelled).

timezone.description: IANA zone for local times, e.g. 'Europe/Paris'. Optional: resolved from the coordinates (with its historical DST rules).

tools.name: seasons
tools.description: Equinoxes and solstices of a year, Earth's perihelion and aphelion, and optionally the Sun day by day (sunrise, sunset, day length, declination, equation of time) for a place. E.g. {year: 2026}. For calendars, almanacs, education and solar apps: the March and September equinoxes and the June and December solstices (UTC, and local with a place), Earth's perihelion and aphelion with their distances, and with daily=true a row per day: solar noon, the Sun's apparent declination, the equation of time and, for a place, sunrise, sunset and day length, plus the longest and shortest days. Matches the published 2026 times to the minute. Deterministic (JPL DE440, no LLM); every result carries meta.result_sha256. Price $0.01 per call via REST POST https://astro-agent.dev/v1/astronomy/seasons (x402 or MPP); each client gets 1 free call on the $0.01-0.02 tools, this one included.

latitude.description: Optional: local times, and with daily=true the day-by-day sunrise, sunset and day length at this place.

elevation_m.description: Height above the WGS84 ellipsoid, metres (no terrain or horizon dip is modelled).

timezone.description: IANA zone for local times, e.g. 'Europe/Paris'. Optional: resolved from the coordinates (with its historical DST rules).

daily.description: Add one row per day: solar noon, the Sun's declination, the equation of time and, with a place, sunrise, sunset and day length.

tools.name: time_scales
tools.description: Julian day, modified Julian day, sidereal time (Greenwich and local, mean and apparent), Delta T, TAI-UTC and UT1-UTC for a moment. E.g. {datetime: '2026-06-21T12:00:00Z', longitude: 2.35, latitude: 48.86}. For telescope control, data reduction and education: the Julian day in UTC, UT1, TT and TDB, the modified Julian day, Julian centuries since J2000 (TT), Delta T (TT - UT1), TAI - UTC and UT1 - UTC, Greenwich mean and apparent sidereal time and, with a longitude, the local ones; plus day of year and ISO week. Deterministic (JPL DE440, no LLM); every result carries meta.result_sha256. Price $0.01 per call via REST POST https://astro-agent.dev/v1/astronomy/time (x402 or MPP); each client gets 1 free call on the $0.01-0.02 tools, this one included.

datetime.description: The moment: UTC ('2026-06-21T12:00:00Z'), with an explicit offset, or local civil time with latitude/longitude.

latitude.description: Optional: resolve a local time, and give the local sidereal time.

timezone.description: IANA zone for local times, e.g. 'Europe/Paris'. Optional: resolved from the coordinates (with its historical DST rules).

tools.name: convert_coordinates
tools.description: Convert sky coordinates between equatorial (J2000, of date), ecliptic, galactic and horizontal (alt-az) frames. E.g. {frame: 'equatorial_j2000', coordinates: {ra_hours: 6.7525, dec: -16.7161}, datetime: '2026-06-21T21:00:00Z', latitude: 48.8566, longitude: 2.3522}. For catalogues, planetarium and telescope software: give a direction in one frame and get it in all the others: equatorial J2000 (ICRS) and of date, ecliptic J2000 and of date, galactic, and horizontal (altitude, azimuth) when a datetime and a place are given. Geometric frame rotations of a direction (no aberration or refraction is added: use astronomy/altaz for where a body appears). Deterministic (JPL DE440, no LLM); every result carries meta.result_sha256. Price $0.01 per call via REST POST https://astro-agent.dev/v1/astronomy/convert (x402 or MPP); each client gets 1 free call on the $0.01-0.02 tools, this one included.

frame.description: The frame of the input coordinates.

longitude.description: Ecliptic and galactic frames: longitude, degrees 0-360.

latitude.description: Ecliptic and galactic frames: latitude, degrees.

azimuth.description: Horizontal frame: azimuth from north, degrees 0-360.

coordinates.description: The direction, with the two fields of its frame.

datetime.description: Needed for the of-date and horizontal frames (UTC, offset, or local time with latitude/longitude).

latitude.description: Observer latitude, for the horizontal frame.

longitude.description: Observer longitude, for the horizontal frame.

tools.name: planetary_phenomena
tools.description: Planetary phenomena between two dates: oppositions, conjunctions with the Sun, greatest elongations of Mercury and Venus, conjunctions between planets, perihelion and aphelion. E.g. {start: '2026-01-01', end: '2026-12-31', include: ['opposition']}. For almanacs, observing guides and astronomy newsletters: between two dates (up to 366 days, 1800-2199), each planet's conjunctions with the Sun, oppositions (with the Earth distance), greatest elongations east or west (with the angle), conjunctions between planets (with their angular separation and distance from the Sun), and perihelion and aphelion (heliocentric distance), each with a stable key. Matches the published 2026 dates. Deterministic (JPL DE440, no LLM); every result carries meta.result_sha256. Price $0.10 per call via REST POST https://astro-agent.dev/v1/astronomy/phenomena (x402 or MPP); always paid, never a free call.

end.description: Last UTC date, YYYY-MM-DD, at most 366 days after start.

tools.name: local_eclipse
tools.description: Solar and lunar eclipses seen from a place: local type, contact times (C1-C4, P1-P4, U1-U4), magnitude, obscuration, duration of totality and the Sun's or Moon's altitude. E.g. {start: '2026-08-01', end: '2026-08-31', latitude: 39.47, longitude: -0.38}. For eclipse chasers, planetariums, schools and travel apps: solar eclipses from the place's own viewpoint (local type: total, annular, partial or none; contacts C1, C2, maximum, C3, C4 with the Sun's altitude and azimuth; magnitude, obscuration, duration, duration of totality or annularity) and lunar eclipses (penumbral and umbral contacts P1, U1, U2, maximum, U3, U4, P4 with the Moon's altitude, umbral and penumbral magnitude, durations), each marked visible when the body is above the horizon. Matches NASA's predictions to a few seconds (2024-04-08 at Dallas, 2025-03-14 lunar eclipse). Deterministic (JPL DE440, no LLM); every result carries meta.result_sha256. Price $0.10 per call via REST POST https://astro-agent.dev/v1/astronomy/eclipse-local (x402 or MPP); always paid, never a free call.

end.description: Last UTC date, YYYY-MM-DD, at most 366 days after start.

elevation_m.description: Height above the WGS84 ellipsoid, metres (no terrain or horizon dip is modelled).

timezone.description: IANA zone for local times, e.g. 'Europe/Paris'. Optional: resolved from the coordinates (with its historical DST rules).

kinds.description: Eclipse kinds to return. Default: both.

tools.name: solunar_periods
tools.description: Solunar periods for a place and day: major periods around the Moon's upper and lower transits, minor periods around moonrise and moonset, in local time. E.g. {date: '2026-06-21', latitude: 48.8566, longitude: 2.3522}. For fishing, hunting and outdoor apps that use the solunar timing convention: for one local day at a place, each major period (centred on the Moon's upper transit overhead and lower transit underfoot, 2 h by default) and minor period (centred on moonrise and moonset, 1 h by default) with its start, centre and end in local time, the Moon's altitude at its transits and its phase. The events are exact (astronomy/rise-set conventions); the windows are the convention's, adjustable. No rating attached. Deterministic (JPL DE440, no LLM); every result carries meta.result_sha256. Price $0.01 per call via REST POST https://astro-agent.dev/v1/astronomy/solunar (x402 or MPP); each client gets 1 free call on the $0.01-0.02 tools, this one included.

date.description: The local calendar day at the place, YYYY-MM-DD (1800-01-02..2199-12-30).

elevation_m.description: Height above the WGS84 ellipsoid, metres (no terrain or horizon dip is modelled).

timezone.description: IANA zone for local times, e.g. 'Europe/Paris'. Optional: resolved from the coordinates (with its historical DST rules).

major_minutes.description: Length of a major period, centred on a lunar transit.

minor_minutes.description: Length of a minor period, centred on moonrise or moonset.

tools.name: body_positions
tools.description: Planetary positions and ephemeris API (NASA/JPL DE440): the ecliptic longitude, latitude, speed, retrograde flag and distance of the Sun, Moon, planets and lunar nodes at any moment 1800-2200, geocentric or heliocentric, ecliptic or equatorial (right ascension, declination). E.g. {datetime: '2026-10-01T12:00:00Z'}. Geocentric apparent positions from NASA/JPL DE440 (true ecliptic and equinox of date, IAU 2006/2000A), with the Moon's ascending and descending nodes and its mean apogee. Location is optional (only used to interpret a local time). Options: 'heliocentric' perspective (seen from the Sun) and 'equatorial' coordinates (right ascension, declination, and whether |declination| exceeds the obliquity). Deterministic (JPL DE440, no LLM); every result carries meta.result_sha256. Price $0.01 per call via REST POST https://astro-agent.dev/v1/astronomy/positions (x402 or MPP); each client gets 1 free call on the $0.01-0.02 tools, this one included.

datetime.description: Local civil date-time, ISO 8601: '1990-05-15T14:30' (local clock time at the place) or with an explicit offset '1990-05-15T14:30:00+02:00'. Alternative: 'date' + 'time'.

time.description: HH:MM or HH:MM:SS, 24 h. Omit if unknown (computed at 12:00 with a TIME_UNKNOWN warning).

timezone.description: IANA zone, e.g. 'Asia/Kolkata'. Optional: resolved from the coordinates, with the historical offset (DST, Local Mean Time) of that date.

time_basis.description: What the given clock time is: civil wall-clock (default), UTC, Local Mean Time, or true (apparent) solar time.

ambiguous_time.description: Which occurrence to use when a local time happens twice (DST fall-back).

bodies.description: 'all' or a list from ['sun', 'moon', 'mercury', 'venus', 'mars', 'jupiter', 'saturn', 'uranus', 'neptune', 'pluto', 'lunar_node_true', 'lunar_node_true_descending', 'lunar_node_mean', 'lunar_apogee_mean']. Default: the Sun, the Moon, Mercury..Pluto, the Moon's true ascending node, its descending node and its mean apogee.

perspective.description: 'geocentric' (default) or 'heliocentric' (geometric, seen from the Sun: the Earth instead of the Sun and the Moon, no lunar points).

coordinates.description: 'ecliptic' (default: longitude/latitude) or 'equatorial': also each body's right ascension, declination, their daily speeds and whether |declination| exceeds the obliquity of the ecliptic.

tools.name: sky_now
tools.description: The sky now (no location needed): planet positions, retrograde planets and the Moon phase, plus the exact UTC minute of the next stations, lunations and separations. E.g. {datetime: '2026-10-01T00:00Z', days: 30}. One call for 'what is happening in the sky': positions, retrograde planets, the Moon's phase, and the events of the next days (1-90): stations, lunations, separations of 0, 60, 90, 120 and 180 degrees, and ecliptic longitudes crossing multiples of 30 degrees, each to the minute (UTC). Deterministic (JPL DE440, no LLM); every result carries meta.result_sha256. Price $0.01 per call via REST POST https://astro-agent.dev/v1/astronomy/sky (x402 or MPP); each client gets 1 free call on the $0.01-0.02 tools, this one included.

datetime.description: Local civil date-time, ISO 8601: '1990-05-15T14:30' (local clock time at the place) or with an explicit offset '1990-05-15T14:30:00+02:00'. Alternative: 'date' + 'time'.

time.description: HH:MM or HH:MM:SS, 24 h. Omit if unknown (computed at 12:00 with a TIME_UNKNOWN warning).

timezone.description: IANA zone, e.g. 'Asia/Kolkata'. Optional: resolved from the coordinates, with the historical offset (DST, Local Mean Time) of that date.

time_basis.description: What the given clock time is: civil wall-clock (default), UTC, Local Mean Time, or true (apparent) solar time.

ambiguous_time.description: Which occurrence to use when a local time happens twice (DST fall-back).

days.description: How many days ahead to list events. Example: 30.

tools.name: angular_separations
tools.description: Angular separations between planets at a moment, or between longitudes you supply: the pairs near 0, 60, 90, 120 or 180 degrees (or any angle you choose) with the deviation, approaching or receding; optionally equal and opposite declinations. E.g. {longitudes: {sun: 54.4, moon: 297.4}}. For a moment (computed from DE440) or for longitudes you supply: every pair of bodies at a chosen separation angle, with its deviation from the exact angle, the tolerance applied, and whether the bodies are approaching or receding from it. Option 'declination': pairs with equal or opposite declinations. Deterministic (JPL DE440, no LLM); every result carries meta.result_sha256. Price $0.02 per call via REST POST https://astro-agent.dev/v1/astronomy/angles (x402 or MPP); each client gets 1 free call on the $0.01-0.02 tools, this one included.

datetime.description: Local civil date-time, ISO 8601: '1990-05-15T14:30' (local clock time at the place) or with an explicit offset '1990-05-15T14:30:00+02:00'. Alternative: 'date' + 'time'.

time.description: HH:MM or HH:MM:SS, 24 h. Omit if unknown (computed at 12:00 with a TIME_UNKNOWN warning).

timezone.description: IANA zone, e.g. 'Asia/Kolkata'. Optional: resolved from the coordinates, with the historical offset (DST, Local Mean Time) of that date.

time_basis.description: What the given clock time is: civil wall-clock (default), UTC, Local Mean Time, or true (apparent) solar time.

ambiguous_time.description: Which occurrence to use when a local time happens twice (DST fall-back).

longitudes.description: Optional {body: degrees} or {body: {longitude, speed, declination?, declination_speed?}}; when given, no ephemeris is used.

bodies.description: 'all' or a list from ['sun', 'moon', 'mercury', 'venus', 'mars', 'jupiter', 'saturn', 'uranus', 'neptune', 'pluto', 'lunar_node_true', 'lunar_node_true_descending', 'lunar_node_mean', 'lunar_apogee_mean']. Default: the Sun, the Moon, Mercury..Pluto, the Moon's true ascending node, its descending node and its mean apogee.

angles.description: Separation angles in degrees, 'all' or a list from [0, 30, 45, 60, 72, 90, 120, 135, 144, 150, 180]. Default: [0, 60, 90, 120, 180].

tolerances.description: Tolerance in degrees per angle, e.g. {"90": 6}. Defaults: 0 and 180: 8; 90 and 120: 7; 60: 5; the others: 2.

sun_moon_tolerance_bonus.description: Extra tolerance in degrees when either body is the Sun or the Moon.

declination.description: Also return the declinations and the pairs with equal or opposite declinations.

declination_tolerance.description: Tolerance in degrees for equal / opposite declinations.

tools.name: celestial_events
tools.description: Celestial event calendar: the exact UTC minute and unix timestamp of every solar and lunar eclipse, planetary station (retrograde / direct), lunation and separation between two dates, 1800-2200. E.g. {start: '2026-01-01', end: '2026-12-31', include: ['eclipse', 'station']}. A calendar of exact events between two dates: solar and lunar eclipses (type and magnitude), stations (retrograde / direct), new and full Moons and quarters, separations between planets at chosen angles, ecliptic longitudes crossing multiples of 30 degrees, equal / opposite declinations, and declinations passing the obliquity of the ecliptic. Geocentric or heliocentric. Each event has its UTC minute, a unix timestamp and a stable key. Deterministic (JPL DE440, no LLM); every result carries meta.result_sha256. Price $0.25 per call via REST POST https://astro-agent.dev/v1/astronomy/events (x402 or MPP); always paid, never a free call.

end.description: Last UTC date, YYYY-MM-DD, at most 366 days after start (inclusive).

perspective.description: 'geocentric' (default) or 'heliocentric'. Heliocentric gives separations and longitude crossings only (no stations, lunations or eclipses).

bodies.description: Planets searched. Default: Sun..Pluto (geo), Mercury..Pluto with Earth (helio).

include_moon.description: Also the Moon's separations, longitude crossings and declination events (geocentric only; many more events).

include.description: Event types. Default: all that apply to the perspective. 'separation': two bodies reach one of the 'angles'; 'longitude_crossing': a body's ecliptic longitude crosses a multiple of 30 degrees; 'declination': equal or opposite declinations; 'declination_beyond_obliquity': |declination| passes the obliquity of the ecliptic; 'station', 'lunation', 'eclipse'.

angles.description: Separation angles in degrees, 'all' or a list from [0, 30, 45, 60, 72, 90, 120, 135, 144, 150, 180]. Default: [0, 60, 90, 120, 180].

tools.name: longitude_series
tools.description: Planetary longitude time series: planet degrees seen from the Earth and from the Sun (geocentric and heliocentric) at a moment or every hour to every week, as pandas-ready columns, with speeds, retrograde flags and declinations. E.g. {start: '2024-01-01', end: '2024-12-31', interval: '1w', bodies: ['jupiter', 'saturn']}. Planetary longitudes as data: at a moment, or as a series of up to 1000 samples (columns ready for pandas). Geocentric apparent and heliocentric geometric, each with its speed and retrograde flag; optional offsets (longitude + angle), circular or arithmetic multi-body averages, unwrapped degrees for plotting, and declinations. Deterministic (JPL DE440, no LLM); every result carries meta.result_sha256. Price $0.20 per call via REST POST https://astro-agent.dev/v1/astronomy/longitude-series (x402 or MPP); always paid, never a free call.

datetime.description: A moment (snapshot): ISO 8601 with Z or an offset, e.g. '2024-01-01T00:00Z'. A local time needs 'timezone' or coordinates. Omit when giving start/end.

timezone.description: IANA zone, e.g. 'Asia/Kolkata'. Optional: resolved from the coordinates, with the historical offset (DST, Local Mean Time) of that date.

start.description: Series: first UTC date, YYYY-MM-DD. Example: '2024-01-01'.

end.description: Series: last UTC date, YYYY-MM-DD (at most 1000 samples).

interval.description: Series sampling step: 1 hour, 4 hours, 12 hours, 1 day or 1 week.

time_utc.description: Series: UTC time of day of the first sample, HH:MM.

perspective.description: Geocentric, heliocentric, or both in one call (default).

bodies.description: Bodies. Default: Sun..Pluto (geocentric), Mercury..Pluto with the Earth (heliocentric).

offsets.description: Angles in degrees added to every longitude (+angle and -angle), 'all' or a list from [0, 30, 45, 60, 72, 90, 120, 135, 144, 150, 180]. Default: none (the longitude itself).

averages.description: Multi-body longitude averages: mean_of_5 = (Jupiter+Saturn+Uranus+Neptune+Pluto)/5, circle_of_8 = (Mercury+Venus+Mars+Jupiter+Saturn+Uranus+Neptune+Pluto)/8, in each perspective.

average_method.description: 'arithmetic' mean of the 0-360 longitude values or 'circular' (vector) mean of the directions.

include_declination.description: Series: also a declination column per body.

format.description: Series layout: 'columns' (pandas.DataFrame(result['series'])) or 'rows' (one object per sample).

unwrap.description: Series: continuous degrees (no 360 -> 0 jump), for plotting.

tools.name: similar_skies
tools.description: Sky similarity search: find the past or future dates whose planetary positions best match a reference sky, ranked by a stated angular distance in degrees. E.g. {reference: '2026-10-29T00:00Z', direction: 'past', bodies: ['jupiter', 'saturn']}. Searches a date grid (1 hour to 1 week steps, 1800-2200) for the skies closest to a reference: by longitude, by the separations between bodies, by declination, optionally with the same retrograde flags. The score is a weighted mean angular distance in degrees, defined in result.settings.metric. Data for your own analysis — never a signal or forecast. Deterministic (JPL DE440, no LLM); every result carries meta.result_sha256. Price $0.25 per call via REST POST https://astro-agent.dev/v1/astronomy/sky-analogues (x402 or MPP); always paid, never a free call.

reference.description: The sky to match: 'now' (default; the current UTC hour or day, echoed in result.reference.date_utc), a UTC moment ('2026-10-29T00:00Z' or 'YYYY-MM-DD'), {datetime: ...}, your own values {values: {feature id: value}} (add 'datetime' to anchor direction and range at a time), or a local date-time and place {place: {datetime: local '1990-05-15T14:30', latitude, longitude, timezone?}}: the time zone comes from the coordinates or 'timezone'; a date alone means 12:00 local with a TIME_UNKNOWN warning. meta.reference_resolution gives the equivalent {values, datetime} request. Feature ids: '<geo|helio>.<body>' (longitude, 0-360), '<geo|helio>.<a>-<b>:angle' (separation, 0-180), '<geo|helio>.<body>:declination' (degrees) and 'geo.<body>:retrograde'.

direction.description: Search before the reference (with a local date-time and place: before that moment), after it, or both (default; the only choice with reference.values without 'datetime').

range.description: Candidate dates. Default (a reference with a time): the longest window the caps allow, up to 100 years in the chosen direction (50 on each side for 'both').

resolution.description: Step of the candidate grid. At most 36,600 candidate dates per call, and at most 660,000 dates x ephemeris series (one per body and perspective, plus one per retrograde-flagged body).

perspective.description: Positions seen from the Earth, from the Sun, or both.

bodies.description: Bodies to match. Default: Sun..Pluto (geo), Mercury..Pluto with Earth (helio).

features.description: What to compare: 'longitude' (default), 'separations' (the angle between every pair of bodies), 'declination', 'retrograde' (a filter on equal retrograde flags).

weights.description: Optional {feature id: weight}, default 1 each, e.g. {'geo.jupiter': 2}. Feature ids: '<geo|helio>.<body>' (longitude, 0-360), '<geo|helio>.<a>-<b>:angle' (separation, 0-180), '<geo|helio>.<body>:declination' (degrees) and 'geo.<body>:retrograde' (true/false).

max_distance.description: Optional: only matches whose score (degrees) is at most this.

min_separation_days.description: Minimum gap between two matches and between a match and the reference time, so one passage gives one match. Raise it (e.g. 3650) to skip the current cycle of slow planets.

require_same_retrograde.description: Keep only dates whose retrograde flags equal the reference's.

tools.name: resolve_local_time
tools.description: Local time to UTC conversion: convert a local date, time and place into exact Universal Time, with the historical time zone and UTC offset, Delta T, Local Mean Time and true solar time. E.g. {datetime: '1947-08-15T00:00', latitude: 28.6139, longitude: 77.209}. Resolves the IANA time zone from coordinates, applies the offset in force on that date (historical daylight saving, Local Mean Time before standard time), flags ambiguous or non-existent local times instead of guessing, and returns Julian Days (UT/TT), Delta T, Local Mean Time, true (apparent) solar time and the equation of time. Deterministic (JPL DE440, no LLM); every result carries meta.result_sha256. Price $0.01 per call via REST POST https://astro-agent.dev/v1/astronomy/local-time (x402 or MPP); each client gets 1 free call on the $0.01-0.02 tools, this one included.

datetime.description: Local civil date-time, ISO 8601: '1990-05-15T14:30' (local clock time at the place) or with an explicit offset '1990-05-15T14:30:00+02:00'. Alternative: 'date' + 'time'.

time.description: HH:MM or HH:MM:SS, 24 h. Omit if unknown (computed at 12:00 with a TIME_UNKNOWN warning).

timezone.description: IANA zone, e.g. 'Asia/Kolkata'. Optional: resolved from the coordinates, with the historical offset (DST, Local Mean Time) of that date.

time_basis.description: What the given clock time is: civil wall-clock (default), UTC, Local Mean Time, or true (apparent) solar time.

ambiguous_time.description: Which occurrence to use when a local time happens twice (DST fall-back).

inputSchema.description: Coordinates or a timezone are needed to interpret a local time.

tools.name: astro_catalog
tools.description: List every astronomical data and ephemeris tool with its price, input schema and an example request: planet positions, event calendar (eclipses, Mercury retrograde), longitude series, sky similarity search and more. Free; call it first to pick the right tool.

tools.name: verify_result_hash
tools.description: Verify that an astronomical data result was not altered: recompute the SHA-256 of a 'result' object returned by any tool and compare it with the result_sha256 you hold. Free.

result.description: The 'result' object exactly as a tool returned it.

result_sha256.description: The meta.result_sha256 returned with it (64 hex characters). Omit to only recompute the hash.
